title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X/S is a smooth relative curve with ω = Ω^1_{X/S} invertible. V (written J on the previous page) is a rank-3 bundle with a three-step filtration Ω ⊂ L ⊂ V. Its graded pieces are gr_1 = Ω, gr_2 = Ω^0 = O_X, gr_3 = Ω^{-1}. V carries a Lie bracket: the previous page remarks on derivations of J, and the terms [ϖ_i, λδ] here are brackets. So V is a twisted form of sl_2, i.e. an adjoint/Sym^2-type bundle (weights 2, 0, -2), with a filtration by a line subbundle Ω and a rank-2 L = Ω^⊥.

Connections. After choosing a splitting V ≅ Ω ⊕ O ⊕ Ω^{-1} and a local basis δ of Ω, there is a trivial connection c_0 with c_0(λδ + μ + νδ^{-1}) = δdλ + dμ + δ^{-1}dν. Every connection is c_ϖ = c_0 + ad(ϖ) with ϖ = ϖ_2 + ϖ_1 + ϖ_0 ∈ Γ(V⊗ω), where ϖ_2 ∈ Γ(Ω⊗ω), ϖ_1 ∈ Γ(ω), ϖ_0 ∈ Γ(Ω^{-1}⊗ω).

Computation on this page. He computes c_ϖ on w_1 = λδ, w_0 = μ·1 and w_{-1} = νδ^{-1}. He gets formulas such as c(w_1) = δdλ + w_1(ϖ_1 − 2ϖ_0), keeping track of weights.

Conclusion. Every connection satisfies the transversality c(Fil_i) ⊂ Fil_{i-1}(V⊗ω). The induced graded maps c_{i,i+1}: gr_i → gr_{i+1}⊗ω are O-linear and depend only on ϖ_0:
- c_{1,2} = −2ϖ_0 : Ω → ω;
- c_{2,3} = ϖ_0 : O → Ω^{-1}⊗ω.
Hence c_{1,2} = −2c_{2,3}, which is independent of the splittings.

NB on filtration-preserving connections. Connections preserving the filtration are those with ϖ_0 = 0. Equivalently they preserve L, or equivalently the section σ of the associated P^1-bundle P is horizontal. They form a torsor under L⊗ω.

Torsor structure. The space Conn of (Lie-compatible) connections is a torsor under V⊗ω. Pushing out along V⊗ω → Ω^{-1}⊗ω gives the canonical map Conn → Ω^{-1}⊗ω, c ↦ ϖ_0(c). Fixing ϖ_0(c) reduces the structure group to L⊗ω. Pushing further along L⊗ω → ω gives a torsor under ω.
- These classes are the restrictions c_Ω : Ω → L⊗ω of connections compatible with a given i.
- Each c_Ω is an additive first-order differential operator: c_Ω(fw) − f c_Ω(w) = w⊗df.
- Its composite Ω → L⊗ω → ω is linear and equal to −2i.

Next page. He imposes that Ω → ω be an isomorphism. This is the Kodaira–Spencer / oper non-degeneracy condition. He then identifies the data canonically from X/S: L ≅ P^1_{X/S}(ω)⊗ω^{-1}, so L⊗ω ≅ P^1(ω), and c_Ω is essentially the universal first-order principal-part map d^1.

Purpose and context. This is the structure of Sym^2 / adjoint bundles of a rank-2 de Rham bundle with Hodge filtration, e.g. H^1_dR of a family of elliptic curves with the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism ω_E^2 ≅ Ω^1. In modern terms these are PGL_2-opers / indigenous bundles / projective structures, presumably prepared for Gauss–Manin and Cartier-operator (p-curvature) questions in this dossier.
errors: The numerical ratio c_{1,2} = −2 c_{2,3} depends on how gr_2 is identified with O_X and on the bracket normalization. With the standard sl_2 basis (e, h, f), one finds ad(ϖ_0 f)(e) = −ϖ_0 h and ad(ϖ_0 f)(h) = 2ϖ_0 f, giving ratio −1/2 rather than −2. Grothendieck's factor reflects his particular identification and is not intrinsic; that both maps are determined by the single class ϖ_0 is intrinsic.

Several formulas are written schematically (e.g. 'c(w_1) = δdλ + w_1(ϖ_1 − 2ϖ_0)') and do not separate graded components. Only the gr-components are used in the conclusion, so no substantive gap results.

ideas.what: Connections on a filtered rank-3 (twisted sl_2) bundle satisfy automatic transversality; the graded pieces are O-linear and governed by a single canonical class ϖ_0, independent of splitting
ideas.modern_name: Griffiths transversality / oper structure for PGL_2 (Sym^2 of a rank-2 oper)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths (transversality, 1968); Drinfeld–Sokolov (1985) and Beilinson–Drinfeld (1990s) for opers; Gunning (1967) for indigenous bundles

ideas.what: Torsor description of the space of connections and its successive reductions of structure group (V⊗ω → L⊗ω → ω); horizontality of the section σ of the P^1-bundle
ideas.modern_name: Affine space of opers / projective structures as a torsor under quadratic differentials; flat P^1-bundle with section

ideas.what: Non-degeneracy condition (Ω → ω an isomorphism) with canonical model L⊗ω ≅ P^1_{X/S}(ω) and c_Ω induced by d^1 (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism; jet-bundle construction of the canonical oper filtration
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz (1973, p-adic modular forms: ω^2 ≅ Ω^1); Beilinson–Drinfeld; classical projective-structure theory

missed.claim: Grothendieck, around 1972 and in a dossier on Gauss–Manin and the Cartier operation, sets up the oper / indigenous-bundle formalism for PGL_2 relative to an arbitrary smooth curve X/S. The ingredients are: a filtered sl_2-bundle; the canonical class ϖ_0 governing all graded Kodaira–Spencer maps; reduction of the connection torsor; and identification via P^1(ω). Combined with the Cartier operator, this is the framework later used for p-curvature of opers (Mochizuki's dormant indigenous bundles, p-adic Teichmüller theory).
missed.quote: si c section de Conn, ϖ_0(c) détermine les homs gr_i(V) → gr_{i+1}(V⊗ω)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents an early, relative, characteristic-free treatment of projective structures linked to Gauss–Manin and Cartier operations. It predates the Beilinson–Drinfeld oper language and Mochizuki's indigenous bundles in char p; of historical rather than new-mathematical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is essentially the standard structure of PGL_2-opers and the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism, all now textbook. It is mildly notable as an unpublished early (c.1972) relative formulation tied to Gauss–Manin and Cartier operations, anticipating later oper / indigenous-bundle language.
transcription_corrections: 'c_{ϖ_x}' is c_ϖ (connection defined by ϖ); the subscript is not x.
The arguments 'ω_1, ω_0, ω_{-1}' are elements w_1 = λδ, w_0 = μ·1, w_{-1} = νδ^{-1} (the image shows 'λδ', 'μ.1', 'νδ^{-1}' written under them), not differential forms.
First line second row: '+ ϖ_1(λδ) − 2ϖ_0(λδ)' with 'poids 2' annotations under δdλ and ϖ_1(λδ).
'V' is the script letter used for the rank-3 bundle (J on the previous page), with V : Ω, Ω^0 = O_X, Ω^{-1}; the second line reads 'V⊗ω : Ω⊗ω, ω, Ω^{-1}⊗ω'.
In 'Re NB', 'L' ≅ L⊗Ω^{-1}' likely reads 'L^⊥ ≅ L⊗Ω^{-1}' or similar; uncertain.
